questions.q: How is financial data in Oracle Fusion primarily organized?
options: By subledger — each module owns its own transaction tables
In one single table for all transactions
By the user who entered the data
Alphabetically by table name
questions.explain: Each module (Payables, Receivables, Fixed Assets, Cash Management, Expenses) owns the detailed transaction tables for its own area of the business.

questions.q: What does the table prefix usually tell you?
options: Which database server the table is on
Which module owns the table, e.g. AP_ for Payables, AR_ for Receivables
The table's creation date
Nothing — prefixes are random
questions.explain: Oracle Fusion table names are prefixed by module: AP_ Payables, AR_ Receivables, FA_ Fixed Assets, CE_ Cash Management, XLA_ Subledger Accounting, HZ_ Trading Community Architecture.

questions.q: What is Subledger Accounting (SLA), and what prefix do its tables use?
options: A legacy module no longer used in Fusion
A reporting tool with no tables of its own
The shared engine that converts subledger transactions into GL journal entries, prefixed XLA_
Another name for the General Ledger itself
questions.explain: Every subledger — Payables, Receivables, Fixed Assets and more — routes through the same Subledger Accounting engine (XLA_ tables) before reaching GL.

questions.q: Why does Oracle Fusion store supplier and customer identity data separately from AP and AR transactions?
options: For performance reasons only, with no business meaning
Because suppliers and customers never share any structure
It doesn't — identity is duplicated separately inside AP and AR
Because a party (company or person) is a shared concept that can hold a supplier role, a customer role, or both, without duplicating the core identity
questions.explain: Trading Community Architecture (HZ_ tables) stores the core party identity once; supplier and customer roles are layered on top, so the same real-world company isn't duplicated if it's both.

questions.q: What is the correct high-level flow from a subledger transaction to the General Ledger?
options: Subledger transaction, then subledger accounting event, then GL journal entry
Subledger transaction directly becomes a GL journal entry with no intermediate step
There is no defined flow — each module posts independently
GL journal entry, then subledger accounting event, then subledger transaction
questions.explain: A subledger transaction generates a subledger accounting event (XLA_), which produces the GL journal entry (GL_) — this flow repeats across every subledger.
